text:
alex_g: FYI I'm onboarding a new upstream model 'tempest-11b' for benchmark/quant experiments. README has a weird clause: 'non-commercial use; no redistribution of modified or quantized weights'. Want to confirm allowable experimenation for hosted evals and internal devs.

sara_legal: Can you paste the exact clause? If it explicitly forbids redistribution of modified weights we can't publish quantized checkpoints or share them externally. Hosting a model behind our API is usually OK if not distributing weights, but need to check 'commercial use' wording for product demos.

alex_g: snippet from README: 
```
License: TEMP-L v0.9
Permissions: research, evaluation, display
Restrictions: no commercial use, no redistribution of model weights or derivative checkpoints; attribution required when results are published
```

mohit_ml: That sounds like a non-commercial license. We can do internal quant experiments and run evals on our infra, but cannot ship quantized weights with any user-facing product. Also watch out: 'attribution required' might apply to embeddings/api responses in publications.

jason_quant: For the quant pipeline I'm planning: `python quantize.py --model=tempest-11b --bits=4 --out=tempest-11b-4bit.pt` — we'll run locally on dedicated infra. But if the license disallows redistribution, we need to mark the model registry entry as "no_share" and block export from Redwood Dedicated/private bundles.

emma_ops: From an ops perspective: hosting is feasible behind our hosted API as long as we don't provide download links. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers though, giving them a package containing weights could violate the license unless we get permission. Also make sure KMS keys for any artifacts are customer-managed when required.

sara_legal: Options: 1) Treat as research-only: internal evals + no public/demo usage; 2) Ask upstream for a commercial/redistribution exception or a different license; 3) Use the model only for evaluation benches and keep any artifacts gated (no bundling/export). I'll draft an outreach template to request permission — need contact and SPDX or original repo link.

alex_g: repo: https://repo.example/tempest-11b, contact: maintainer @tempest-team (email in repo). I'll add the SPDX and the README to the model registry metadata.

mohit_ml: Also note quality/regression risk: our eval suite (evalset id: 214) shows 2.3% BLEU drop when going 8->4 bit on similar archs. If we can't publish quantized weights, we should still publish a short note in our benchmarks about quantized performance but avoid distributing artifacts.

jason_quant: Agreed — we can publish inference numbers and config (quant settings) but not checkpoints. For reproducibility, include the exact commit hash and quant script snippet, not the weight files.

emma_ops: Let's add a license flag to the onboarding flow: `license.can_redistribute_weights=false`, `license.non_commercial=true`, `license.attribution_required=true`. That will drive UI and deployment blockers.

license-bot: auto-detect: TEMP-L v0.9 -> flags set: can_redistribute_weights:false, commercial_use:false, attribution:true. Flagged for legal review.

sara_legal: I'll reach out to maintainers asking for clarification and a waiver for redistribution if possible. Meanwhile set registry flags and block push to public artifact store. If they grant an exception, we'll require an explicit signed addendum and update onboarding docs.

alex_g: OK I'm going to: 1) run local quant evals on dev cluster (no sharing), 2) add license metadata to registry, 3) ping upstream via legal template. Will update thread with responses. Thanks. :thumbsup:
